prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick a single “best” company for you without knowing your exact location and priorities, and local reputations change over time — but I can help you find a top-quality Miami installer and give you the checklist to make a confident choice.

Key things to look for in a hurricane-rated roofing contractor
- Proper licensing and insurance
  - Florida DBPR (Construction) license and current status
  - General liability and workers’ comp coverage
- Proven hurricane/HVHZ experience
  - Experience working in Miami-Dade County’s High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ)
  - Knowledge of Miami‑Dade County product approvals and Florida Building Code requirements
- Product approvals and manufacturer certifications
  - Use of Miami‑Dade NOA‑approved roofing products or systems
  - Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc.) matter for warranties
- Wind-uplift and attachment systems
  - Contractor should specify uplift rating and fastener/adhesive details; ask for engineered uplift calculations if needed
- Warranties and workmanship guarantees
  - Distinguish manufacturer warranty from contractor workmanship warranty and get both in writing
- Local references and reviews
  - Recent Miami-area projects, ideally in HVHZ areas; check Google, Yelp, BBB, and ask for photos and referrals
- Permitting and inspections
  - Contractor should obtain permits and arrange final inspections; do not proceed without proper permits
- Payment terms and lien releases
  - Avoid full upfront payments; require lien waivers when progress payments are made

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida and registered to work in Miami-Dade County? Can I see the license number?
- Which products you install have Miami‑Dade NOAs? Can you provide the NOA numbers?
- What wind speed and uplift rating will this roof be designed for?
- Are you certified by the roof system/manufacturer? What warranties will I get?
- Do you routinely handle insurance claims? Can you provide references from recent hurricane-rated installs?
- Who will pull the permit and handle inspections?
- What is your payment schedule and do you provide lien releases?

Materials and systems that perform well in hurricanes
- Properly installed metal (standing seam, mechanically attached or concealed-clip systems)
- Concrete or clay tile with engineered straps and adequately rated underlayment
- Modified bitumen or mechanically attached TPO/EPDM with appropriate uplift systems for low-slope roofs
(Performance depends on correct fastening and flashing, not just material.)

Avoid
- Storm‑chasers or contractors who pressure you to sign immediately
- Contractors without local HVHZ experience or without Miami‑Dade NOA products
- Large upfront cash payments without a written contract and lien waivers

If you want, I can:
- Pull together a short vetted list of Miami roofing companies with strong hurricane experience (I’ll need your zip code)
- Review estimates or contracts you receive and point out red flags

Which would you prefer — a shortlist for your area, or help evaluating bids you already have?
